endpoints.contract_notes: backup_type full (default) or incremental; atomic admission shared by both types. 409 backup_in_progress while a backup is pending/in_progress, database_busy for nonterminal work on the actual source VM, restore_not_activated for a restore-to-new database not activated, recovery_in_progress or pitr_reopen_in_progress during recovery/PITR reopen. Incremental-only refusals: incremental_requires_policy, incremental_not_supported_on_replica, incremental_requires_pitr, incremental_requires_full_backup, incremental_parent_unavailable; never silently falls back to full. Refusals carry success:false, reason and message. A transport error, 5xx, 408/429 or invalid node ACK does not prove refusal; backup/task reservations can remain pending until a terminal callback or operator reconciliation. The user API returns 200 success:false with message for caught dispatch failures; the admin API maps that body to 400. No generic dispatch reason is promised. Inspect backup/task state before retrying; acceptance is not completion. Pending/in_progress backups are conservatively serialized across the primary and all its replicas because historical source VM ownership is not stored. A retained backup of another family member answers 409 database_busy even when its source Task is missing or terminal, regardless of current replica health; distinct sibling source VMs are also held until the authoritative backup state is terminal.

endpoints.contract_notes: Bucket names are unique platform-wide: every user, every S3 server, deleted buckets included, enforced by a database key so two simultaneous creates of one name cannot both succeed. A taken or invalid name answers 422 with errors.name (same text for a lost race as for the normal check) and no remote storage call is made. A saved change answers 200 with success true even when the storage server cannot be reached: the body then carries warning and warning_reason "server_check_failed" (the server status holds an error marker until the next check). verify_tls (boolean, default true) controls certificate verification when ssl is on; false is for self-signed lab servers only (rc alias set --insecure).

endpoints.contract_notes: backup_type full (default) or incremental; atomic admission shared by both types. 409 backup_in_progress while a backup is pending/in_progress, database_busy for nonterminal work on the actual source VM, restore_not_activated for a restore-to-new database not activated, recovery_in_progress or pitr_reopen_in_progress during recovery/PITR reopen. Incremental-only refusals: incremental_requires_policy, incremental_not_supported_on_replica, incremental_requires_pitr, incremental_requires_full_backup, incremental_parent_unavailable; never silently falls back to full. Refusals carry success:false, reason and message. A transport error, 5xx, 408/429 or invalid node ACK does not prove refusal; backup/task reservations can remain pending until a terminal callback or operator reconciliation. The user API returns 200 success:false with message for caught dispatch failures; the admin API maps that body to 400. No generic dispatch reason is promised. Inspect backup/task state before retrying; acceptance is not completion. Pending/in_progress backups are conservatively serialized across the primary and all its replicas because historical source VM ownership is not stored. A retained backup of another family member answers 409 database_busy even when its source Task is missing or terminal, regardless of current replica health; distinct sibling source VMs are also held until the authoritative backup state is terminal.

endpoints.contract_notes: Outbound network policy, remove: the sandbox returns to no policy (unrestricted), which is not an allow-default policy. Stored with generation + 1 and pushed by a queued job: 202 until the node confirms, 200 once it has, and 200 with nothing changed when no policy is set. Accepted on a node that lost the capability (the read then says unavailable when an earlier policy may still be in force). 409 egress_policy_terminal for a killed or errored sandbox; 404 sandbox_not_found. Subusers need microvm.manage and, because the verb is DELETE, microvm.delete. OpenTofu: removing the egress_policy attribute calls it.

Outbound network policy, read. 200 {success, egress: {policy, generation, applied_generation, state, applied_at, last_error_code, capability: {available, names}, service_ports: [{proto, port}]}}. policy is null when no policy is set (unrestricted), else {default_action allow|deny, inbound_replies service_ports|any, rules: [{id, action, target, protocol, ports?, comment?}]}. state is none, pending, applied, failed, unavailable or inactive (the sandbox is killed or errored; the stored policy is kept for reading and is in force nowhere; such a sandbox without a policy reads none); last_error_code is the node's typed code when failed or unavailable. Never calls the node. Needs microvm.view. Works in every sandbox state. Unknown, deleted or foreign sandbox: 404 reason sandbox_not_found. OpenTofu: iaas_microvm.egress_policy is refreshed from it (drift detection) and egress_policy_state / egress_policy_generation mirror state and generation.

Outbound network policy, replace. The request body IS the policy document: default_action (required, allow|deny), inbound_replies (optional, service_ports|any; any is refused with deny), rules (optional list, at most 100) of {action allow|deny, target (host name, *.wildcard, IPv4/IPv6 address or CIDR), protocol tcp|udp|icmp|any (default any), ports (numbers, or "lo-hi" ranges on address and CIDR rules), comment, id (assigned when omitted)}. Unknown keys are refused. Stored with generation + 1 and pushed to the node by a queued job, never in the request: 202 while the node has not confirmed the generation (also for a stopped sandbox, which starts with the policy), 200 once it has; the body is the read model of GET. Refusals change nothing: 422 with reason = the first problem's code (invalid_egress_policy, egress_target_invalid, egress_target_not_permitted, egress_wildcard_too_broad, egress_dns_port_not_allowed, egress_rule_limit_exceeded, egress_names_not_supported), errors {field: [messages]} with paths relative to the policy (document-level problems under `policy`) and violations [{code, field, message}]; 409 egress_policy_terminal (killed or errored sandbox); 409 egress_policy_unsupported_node (the node cannot enforce a policy); 404 sandbox_not_found. Needs microvm.manage. No optimistic concurrency (no If-Match) and no PATCH: a replace is whole-document.

Outbound refusal log, read. 200 {success, events: {current_page, data: [...], per_page, total, last_page, ...}, collection: {pulled_at, packet_layer, retention_days, max_rows}}, newest first. Each entry is an aggregate: {id, layer dns|packet, class (default, rule, floor, private, dns_name_denied, dns_cname_denied, dns_floor_stripped, dns_set_full, dns_malformed, suppressed), rule (a rule id, default, or floor:<category>), rule_id, category, destination (a host name for dns, an address for packet, null when withheld), withheld (true for a refusal that hit a platform network; a packet entry of that kind always has class floor, whichever rule of the policy would have dropped it, so class=floor returns every floor refusal), protocol, port, qtype, count, sampled (true only when count may be too low because refusals arrived faster than the node records them; false means count is exact, which dns entries always are), suppressed_keys, first_at, last_at}. rule_id is the deciding customer rule, `default` on every entry the default action decided (dns and packet alike), null otherwise. Query: layer, class, rule_id (rule_id=default returns every default-action refusal), search (destination contains, literal), since and until (ISO 8601 or Unix seconds, on last_at), page, per_page (default 50, capped at 100). A bad filter value is the framework 422 {message, errors}. collection.pulled_at is the last SUCCESSFUL collection, the final one before a stop, kill or delete included. Reads what the Master has stored (collected from the node about once a minute and once more before a stop, kill or delete), never calls the node, works for a killed sandbox; kept 14 days and 5000 entries per sandbox. Only refusals: never allowed traffic, payloads, URLs or DNS answers. Needs microvm.view. Unknown, deleted or foreign sandbox: 404 reason sandbox_not_found.

opentofu.reason: read-only operational log of refused connections, not declarative state: it changes every minute, so a data source would only snapshot a moving list; the policy itself is covered by iaas_microvm.egress_policy

endpoints.contract_notes: Sandbox run API, mint a run token. Body: scopes (required, non-empty subset of exec, files.read, files.write), ttl_seconds (optional, 30 to 900, default 300), auto_resume (optional boolean, default false: a paused sandbox answers 409 sandbox_paused; true resumes it first and answers 409 billing_hold when the sandbox is held). 200 {success, base_url, token, token_type Bearer, expires_at, scopes, sandbox: {id, state}, limits: {foreground_timeout_max_seconds, concurrent_commands, read_max_bytes, write_max_bytes}} with Cache-Control no-store. The caller then talks to the NODE at base_url (`/commands`, `/files/...`, Authorization: Bearer <token>); the node routes are not Master routes and are described by the node's own OpenAPI file, so this manifest cannot cover them. Refusals {success:false, reason, message}: 404 sandbox_not_found (unknown or foreign), 409 sandbox_paused | sandbox_not_running (creating or stopped) | sandbox_killed | envd_not_available (no shell ingress) | billing_hold, 422 validation (scopes, ttl_seconds), 503 node_unsupported (the node does not report system.microvm_runapi === true) | node_domain_missing | node_missing | signing_unavailable, 429 throttle (30 per minute per API key). Needs microvm.manage. A token is bound to the sandbox's current run (stop then start, redeploy and kill make it useless) and is revoked on the node when the minting API key is deleted, disabled or re-scoped, the person is removed or re-roled, or the account is suspended. Audited as microvm.dataplane.access (scopes, ttl, credential id, key id; never the token). opentofu.reason: mints a short-lived bearer credential for imperative guest operations (run a command, read or write a file); it describes no declarative state, and a token kept in state would be a secret that expires within 15 minutes

endpoints.contract_notes: Sandbox run API, mint a preview link for a port. Body: port (required integer; 1024 to 65535 except 49983, else 422 reason port_not_allowed), ttl_seconds (optional, 60 to 86400, default 3600). 200 {success, url, host, port, expires_at, key_id}: url is https://<port>-<sandbox id>.<node domain>/?vc_preview=<token>, a credential (the node swaps it for a host-only cookie on the first request and never passes it to the application); Cache-Control no-store. Works while the sandbox runs the same run it was minted for; a paused sandbox answers 503 on the node (a preview never wakes a sandbox). The port is added to the sandbox's service ports (ingress.preview_ports, at most 8, oldest dropped) and a default-deny outbound policy is re-sent with the new list. Same refusals as the access mint minus auto_resume and billing_hold. Needs microvm.manage; 30 per minute per API key. Audited as microvm.dataplane.preview (port, ttl, credential id, key id; never the URL).

endpoints.contract_notes: Customer disk snapshot. Body: name (required, 1-64 of a-z0-9._-, unique per account), kind (disk; full answers 422 snapshot_kind_unsupported), consistency (auto|quiesced|crash, default auto), description (255), replicate (true answers 422 snapshot_kind_unsupported). Answers 202 {success, snapshot} with status creating: the snapshot turns ready or failed asynchronously, so a client MUST poll GET /microvm/snapshot/{id} (the provider resource and the MCP tool wait). Optional Idempotency-Key header (idempotency.strict). Needs microvm.manage. Checks that need no node are status codes with a reason: 404 sandbox_not_found; 402 insufficient_credit; 409 sandbox_state_invalid, snapshot_in_progress, snapshot_limit, node_snapshots_unsupported; 422 name_taken, snapshot_kind_unsupported and the usual field errors; 429 rate_limited. Before anything is created the location's creation-free pre-check is asked once (3 s, no retry): a refusal it can name is answered at once with the SAME reasons and statuses (409 snapshot_requires_pause with pause_estimate_ms and pause_limit_ms when it reports them, quiesce_unavailable, node_insufficient_disk, sandbox_state_invalid, node_snapshots_unsupported), nothing is created, queued or billed, and nothing is stored under an Idempotency-Key, so the same request (same key) can succeed after the sandbox is paused; when the check passes the 202 carries pause_estimate_ms and pause_limit_ms next to snapshot when it reported them. If the check cannot answer (timeout, connection error, a node without the route, a 5xx, a malformed answer) the request goes ahead unchanged: the node call then runs in a queued job and the same reasons arrive later as a snapshot with status failed, failure_reason and failure_detail {message, pause_estimate_ms and pause_limit_ms when reported}, so a client must still handle both. A running sandbox on a location without a fast-copy file system may pause for a few seconds while its disk is copied (paused_ms, capture_method); pause or resume of the sandbox during that window answers 409 snapshot_in_progress with retryable true and Retry-After 5. The snapshot object has no node id, path or checksum: id, name, description, kind, status (creating|ready|failed|deleting|unavailable), source_sandbox_id (null once the sandbox is deleted), source_state, consistency (quiesced|crash|clean), size_bytes, used_bytes, disk_gib, vcpu, mem_mib, locality, location_id, image_id, capture_method (reflink|paused_copy|offline_copy), paused_ms, volumes_excluded (integer: how many data volumes the sandbox had attached that are NOT in the snapshot, which holds the root disk only; 0 when none), billable_gib, price_gib_hour, failure_reason, failure_detail, created_at, ready_at.

endpoints.contract_notes: New route (it did not exist; the call answered 405). Removes the key's remote user on every enabled storage server and every server of an attached bucket, reads it back as gone, then deletes the key. A storage server that cannot be reached or refuses keeps the key and answers a typed 502 (storage_unreachable or remote_delete_failed); repeat the call. Needs the s3_buckets.delete permission. Also answers 409 reason bucket_busy (nothing changed, repeat) while another access change holds one of the key's buckets. Disabled storage servers are tried best effort after the enabled ones (a failure there is logged and never blocks the delete).

The delete is asynchronous and answers 202 {success, status:'deleting'}. The bucket carries delete_state (null, deleting, failed) and delete_error (typed kind) so a failed delete is visible; DELETE again retries and converges, including for buckets holding unfinished multipart uploads. A delete already running answers 409 reason delete_in_progress. Access is revoked on the storage server (read back) BEFORE billing stops and the job is queued, so a failed delete leaves a bucket nobody can use, never one that is usable and unbilled. If the revoke is not proven nothing is billed or stopped and the call answers 502 reason access_revoke_failed (safe to repeat); a busy bucket answers 409 bucket_busy. The staleness of a running delete is measured from its own heartbeat.
The bucket object includes delete_state (null, deleting, failed) and delete_error (typed kind) so an asynchronous delete that failed is visible; a deleted bucket answers 404.

While another access change (a suspend or resume, a key attach, detach, permission change or delete, an ACL change) holds the bucket, the call answers 409 {success:false, reason:'bucket_busy'} and changed nothing; it is safe to repeat. A bucket mid-suspend or mid-resume also answers bucket_busy to calls that would add access.

While another access change (a suspend or resume, a key attach, detach, permission change or delete, an ACL change) holds the bucket, the call answers 409 {success:false, reason:'bucket_busy'} and changed nothing; it is safe to repeat. A bucket mid-suspend or mid-resume also answers bucket_busy to calls that would add access. The key is re-read under its lock before any remote call: a key that no longer exists answers 404 reason key_not_found, and attaching a deactivated key answers 409 reason key_inactive (no storage call is made in either case). A bucket that is being deleted refuses grant-adding changes.

While another access change (a suspend or resume, a key attach, detach, permission change or delete, an ACL change) holds the bucket, the call answers 409 {success:false, reason:'bucket_busy'} and changed nothing; it is safe to repeat.
